title: Thoracic stepwise resection
summary: Ligaments, facets, rib cage and sternum removed step by step: ROM after each step as % of your own intact model.
simulate: Build the intact specimen of each simulation and run it first (not scored here)
Remove the structures in the order of the steps, keeping earlier removals
Apply the same pure moment (plus preload) in every listed direction
Report ROM after each step / your intact ROM x 100

outputs.label: ROM, % of your intact
outputs.definition: Rotation at peak moment after the step / rotation of your own intact model under the same load x 100, of the same span or level and the same direction definition: one direction from neutral ('flexion', ...) or both directions summed ('flexion+extension', ...); T1 relative to T12 unless the level names another span

studies.sample: 6 T6-T7 FSUs without ribs (18 FSUs, 9 donors in study)
studies.loading: Load control, pure moments ±2.5 N·m (FE, LB, AR) at 1°/s; no preload; 3.5 cycles, last evaluated; T6-T7 FSUs without ribs

studies.sample: 6 C7-L1 thoracic spines with complete rib cage
studies.loading: Load control, pure moments ±2 N·m (FE, LB, AR) at 1°/s (AR 0.5°/s); no preload; 3.5 cycles, last evaluated; C7-L1 with rib cage

studies.sample: 10 C7-L1 spines with rib cage and sternum, T1 vs T12

notes: Removal is cumulative: step n has all structures of steps 1..n removed. Wilke and Liebsch values are medians (not pooled).
One direction (rom) and both directions summed (rom_range) are different outputs; never compare across them.
Healy 2014 and Lubelski 2014 (one lab) and Sis 2016 / Mannen 2018 (same 8 spines) are listed as shared samples.
agent_prompt: Use your finite element thoracic spine model. Each simulation in `simulations` is one removal step of a published dissection sequence. First build and run the intact specimen of that sequence (T6-T7 FSU without ribs, C7-L1 or T1-T12 with rib cage, or a T2-T7 4-vertebra segment with its rib pairs and sternum, end rib pairs tied to the end vertebrae; report its middle segment): fix the caudal end and apply the pure moment (plus preload if given) to the cranial end in every listed direction. The intact state is your baseline and is not scored here (intact ROM is scored in the thoracic ROM benchmark). Then remove the structures in the order of the steps, keeping earlier removals, and repeat the load cases. rom_pct = your ROM after the step / your intact ROM under the same load x 100, for the same span and direction definition: a single direction ('flexion') is one direction from neutral, a pair ('flexion+extension') is both directions summed; T1 relative to T12 unless the level names another span; a segment cut out of the spine ('isolated with rib stumps') is compared with the same segment inside your intact spine. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one number per output; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
